newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin to merge city districts to save money.
newsitem.headline: Berlin to merge city districts to save money.

text.p: Deeply indebted Berlin, bereft of the lavish "frontline" subsidies of Cold War days, wants to merge its 23 city districts into 12 and cut 550 municipal jobs, an official in the German capital said on Wednesday.
The cuts, which would need a two-thirds majority in city hall to push through, would save the struggling city 229 million marks ($148.5 million), interior senator Joerg Schoenbohm said.

The goal would be to divide the city of 3.4 million into 12 districts of roughly 300,000 inhabitants each -- a total that just happens to match the size of Bonn, the sleepy Rhineland town where the federal goverment still resides.

Berlin became the national capital again when Germany reunited in 1990, but parliament has delayed moving until 1999. The city lost its Cold War-era subsidies after 1990 and its municipal debts tripled to more than 50 billion marks.

The city has raised fees for services, turned off lights in some public buildings and shut down escalators in underground rail stations instead of repairing them. If it goes through, the reform will abolish some of the best-known neighbourhood names.
Kreuzberg, the trendiest part of old West Berlin, and the Tiergarten district west of the Brandenburg Gate would merge with the centre of east Berlin under the latter district's name, Mitte (centre).
Pankow, a name once synonymous with communist rule because East Germany's elite settled there in the 1950s, would be swallowed up in a new Weissensee district.

The only other east-west merger would join the working class neighbourhoods of Wedding and Prenzlauer Berg, but that and other new districts would have long double titles that preserve the historic neighbourhood names. ($1=1.5420 Mark)
